claims.text: Atomic-displacement covariance matrices can be computed from ensembles of configurations generated by ab initio molecular dynamics.
Eigenvalues of the displacement covariance matrix can be used to extract an effective vibrational density of states.
The covariance-based approach can evaluate solid-state vibrational entropy with good agreement to experiment.
The demonstrated systems include elemental BCC sodium and FCC aluminum.
The covariance-derived quantum harmonic model incorporates some anharmonicity through temperature-dependent effective vibrational frequencies.
The covariance method does not intrinsically require time evolution, because trajectories are used only to enlarge the configurational ensemble.
Experimental lattice parameters can be used when evaluating force constants to improve treatment of high-temperature expansion.
Short simulations or Monte Carlo sampling are sufficient to obtain a representative covariance matrix.
Averaging over symmetry operations substantially reduces the sampling required.
The covariance matrix encapsulates the vibrational modes and local displacement correlations relevant to entropy.
The method indirectly captures electron–vibration coupling.
The method can recover the full vibrational and relevant anharmonic entropy contributions for both solid and fluid phases.
The method can estimate absolute free energies of both solid and fluid phases near fusion.
Its phase free energies and derived fusion properties will have accuracy comparable to explicit ab initio molecular dynamics and TOR-TILD.
The method will reduce computational cost by an order of magnitude or more.
The method is expected to be most reliable for elemental and binary systems.
The approach may extend to multicomponent high-entropy alloys near fusion.
Performance is contingent on a Gaussian or similar approximation for the atomic-displacement distribution.
Extremely anharmonic fluid phases and multicomponent systems may not have all anharmonic and electron–vibration effects captured exactly.
A side-by-side comparison of solid and liquid free energies, entropy contributions, and fusion temperature against long-run AIMD or TOR-TILD can falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis initially says the method extracts vibrational, anharmonic, and electron–vibration contributions, whereas the intervention limits this to full vibrational and only some anharmonic entropy, the mechanism calls electron–vibration coupling indirect, and the uncertainty field concedes that these effects may not be captured exactly.
